author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces accept an optional specialty filter in the request URL: whole-name, case-insensitive match, not a prefix; an unmatched specialty yields an empty veterinarian list with a successful response; an empty or whitespace value behaves as no filter; without it both surfaces behave as today; the paged surface preserves the filter across pages.
acceptance_criteria: On either surface, a filter naming a held specialty and differing only by letter case lists only veterinarians holding that specialty.
The match is on the whole specialty name, not a prefix: a partial value matches no veterinarian.
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the directory with an empty veterinarian list and a successful response, not an error.
An empty or whitespace-only filter value behaves as if no filter were supplied.
With no filter, both surfaces list every veterinarian as before.
On the paged surface, page-navigation links preserve the active specialty filter.
The machine-readable surface returns the same veterinarians and specialties as the page and is narrowed by the same filter rule.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search remains out of scope (NG-9)
No visible specialty control (form or dropdown) on either surface this round — URL contract only
notes: Filter is a URL contract only. Open questions recorded in the PRD: Unicode vs ASCII case-folding for the match, and behavior when the specialty parameter is supplied more than once. The slice takes the narrowest reading — the owner-search case-folding, and a single filter value — until either resolves.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter is the existing owner-search pattern applied to the veterinarian directory: OwnerRepository/OwnerController already push a filter plus paging down to the query layer and normalize a blank value to no-filter (system-design.md#contracts, OwnerRepository, REQ-OWN-002). VetRepository gains whole-name, case-insensitive specialty-filtered variants of its two read methods; VetController reads an optional specialty request param, treats blank/whitespace as no-filter, and dispatches to the filtered or unfiltered method on each surface. Pushing the match to the query layer (not in-memory) is what keeps paging correct over the filtered set, since totalElements/totalPages come from the filtered Page. No new module, pattern, or integration; NG-9 is already narrowed by the accepted non-goal ADR, so no conflict.
integration_points: VetRepository: add a specialty-filtered paged method (HTML surface) and a specialty-filtered Collection method (JSON surface), matching the whole specialty name case-insensitively via the association Vet.specialties.name
VetController.showVetList: read optional specialty param, blank->no-filter, choose filtered vs findAll(pageable); add specialty to the model so pagination links can carry it
VetController.showResourcesVetList: read optional specialty param, blank->no-filter, choose filtered Collection vs findAll()
vetList.html: pagination hrefs must carry the active specialty, omitted when blank so unfiltered URLs stay unchanged

patterns.description: owner search: blank value normalized to no-filter, then filter+paging delegated to the repository (REQ-OWN-002) -- the precedent this slice mirrors
filter-with-paging query method (findByLastName...) whose returned Page carries filtered totals

risks.risk: Caching the new filtered query methods keys the vets cache on caller-supplied specialty strings, which are unbounded and (given no auth) attacker-controlled -- an unbounded-key memory-growth vector, and eviction is already unconfigured (Open Questions from the Survey #5).
risks.mitigation: Leave the filtered query methods un-@Cacheable; keep caching on the unfiltered reads only. system-design VetRepository row now states the unfiltered reads are cached.

risks.risk: Filtering across the Vet.specialties many-to-many can return duplicate Vet rows from the join.
risks.mitigation: Use a distinct query (derived-name distinct keyword or SELECT DISTINCT in JPQL).

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching must not reintroduce the PostgreSQL owner-search collation defect (Known Defects), which relies on schema/collation for case-folding.
risks.mitigation: Use IgnoreCase matching so the query lower-cases both sides portably, independent of vendor collation; this is the narrowest case-folding reading the PRD open question calls for.

risks.risk: Pagination links that string-concatenate the specialty would not URL-encode it and could break navigation for values with spaces or reserved characters.
risks.mitigation: Build the href with the Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=...)} URL builder, which encodes and omits the param when empty.

notes: ADR index: non-goal ADRs belong in the decision log; added the 2026-08-08 non-goal-vet-directory-filter row to docs/adr/README.md (the index is a standard ADR file, mine to write). system-design.md updated: VetController/VetRepository/Vets Implements now wire REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, and VetController/VetRepository descriptions note the optional specialty filter. Removed the stale Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable route serves no requirement -- REQ-VET-003 reinstated it as a supported surface, which also resolves the Vets '—' Implements inconsistency. REQ-VET-003's JSON route already exists in code (showResourcesVetList) with a passing test; this slice extends both surfaces with the filter. Two PRD open questions are deliberately out of scope for this slice (Unicode vs ASCII case-folding; repeated specialty param) -- the prd-entry takes the narrowest reading and the implementer should not build multi-value or Unicode-fold behavior.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Design-flagged cache memory-growth vector addressed: both new findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase query methods are non-@Cacheable (readOnly @Transactional only); only unfiltered findAll variants keep @Cacheable(vets), so the unbounded caller-supplied specialty never becomes a cache key
No SQL injection: the filter reaches persistence solely via a Spring Data JPA derived query method (parameter-bound), matching the threat model's no-concatenated-SQL invariant

No XSS: caller-supplied specialty flows only into Thymeleaf @{...(specialty=${specialty})} URL expressions which URL-encode query params; no th:utext or reflected raw rendering of the value; the prior literal ?page concatenation was replaced with the safe URL builder
Input normalization treats blank/whitespace-only specialty as no filter, avoiding an empty-string branch into the query
Supply chain unchanged: no build.gradle or dependency edits in the change set
No new privilege boundary crossed: endpoints were already unauthenticated public reads of the vet directory; adding an optional read filter introduces no new authz surface

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods violate the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` BDD naming convention required from 2026-07-31 onward (testing-principles.md § Test Naming). Current names: `shouldFilterVetListBySpecialtyIgnoringCase`, `shouldReturnEmptyVetListForUnknownSpecialty`, `shouldTreatBlankSpecialtyAsNoFilter`, `shouldPreserveSpecialtyAcrossPaginationLinks`, `shouldFilterMachineReadableVetsBySpecialty`. All start with `should` and omit the subject. Rename to the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` form — for example: `theVetListShouldFilterBySpecialtyIgnoringCase`, `theVetListShouldReturnEmptyForUnknownSpecialty`, `theVetListShouldTreatBlankSpecialtyAsNoFilter`, `theVetListShouldPreserveSpecialtyAcrossPaginationLinks`, `theMachineReadableVetListShouldFilterBySpecialty`.
findings.fix: Rename all five test methods to the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` school. The subject disambiguates which surface or component the test covers; without it the name reads like an imperative rather than a specification.

findings.description: All four new test methods violate the same naming convention. Current names: `shouldFilterVetsBySpecialtyIgnoringCaseWithoutDuplicates`, `shouldNotMatchSpecialtyByPrefix`, `shouldReturnEmptyForSpecialtyNoVetHolds`, `shouldFilterPagedVetsBySpecialty`. Rename to — for example: `theVetRepositoryShouldFilterBySpecialtyIgnoringCaseWithoutDuplicates`, `theVetRepositoryShouldNotMatchSpecialtyByPrefix`, `theVetRepositoryShouldReturnEmptyForSpecialtyNoVetHolds`, `theVetRepositoryShouldFilterPagedResultsBySpecialty`.
findings.fix: Apply the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` rename to all four new tests.

findings.description: PRD REQ-VET-004 `Done when` bullet — 'given an empty or whitespace-only filter value, when **either** surface is requested, then the result matches a request with no filter' — is only half-covered. `shouldTreatBlankSpecialtyAsNoFilter` tests the HTML surface (`/vets.html`). The JSON endpoint (`/vets?specialty=   `) is not tested for blank/whitespace treatment. Without this test, a regression on the JSON endpoint blank-filter path would not be caught. Add a controller test: perform GET `/vets` with `accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)` and `param("specialty", "   ")`, expect the full vet list and verify `findAll()` is called instead of `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase`.

author: change-grader
summary: add optional specialty filter to both vet directory surfaces

blast_radius.note: Three production files in the single vet feature package (VetController, VetRepository interface, one Thymeleaf template), roughly 63 added prod lines plus PRD/system-design/ADR docs; no migrations, config, auth, or other sensitive paths touched. Reach is contained to one module.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: normalizeSpecialty maps null/blank to null else strip (blank correctly treated as absent); the derived queries are distinct so the many-to-many join cannot repeat a Vet; filtered reads are deliberately uncached to avoid an unbounded cache key while unfiltered findAll stays cached; the template moves from string concatenation to the Thymeleaf URL builder, which omits a null specialty and leaves unfiltered URLs unchanged. Nothing behaves against its description.

test_adequacy.note: Real DataJpaTest repository tests (no mocks, real H2) assert concrete vet names for ignore-case, no-prefix-match, empty-result, and paged cases; MockMvc controller tests assert real sizes and content and use never()-verifications to prove blank and whitespace values route to findAll rather than the filter, on both surfaces. The boundaries the code changed are exercised, not restated.
